 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the appellant-Insurance Company challenging the judgment and award passed in MVC No.704/2019 dated 30.12.2019 by the Principal District and Sessions Judge and M.A.C.T., Hassan.
2.
Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.
Brief facts of the case are as under:
The claimant was driving the container lorry bearing registration No.KA.19.C.9602 on 17.05.2018 at 5.30 am from Nanjangud to Mangalore via Madikeri.

At that time,

2
the lorry bearing registration No.AP.20.TA.2526 came from opposite side in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the container lorry.
Due to which, the claimant sustained grievous injuries on both legs.
He was immediately shifted to the Hospital, wherein he was treated as inpatient.
Due to the occurrence of accident, he has lost the driving capacity and suffered disability.
Hence, he has filed a claim petition.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.1 remained absent and was placed ex parte.
Respondent No.2- Insurance Company appeared through counsel and filed statement of objection denying the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry.
It is also stated that the accident is in collision between two lorries and there is contributory negligence on the part of both drivers.

The NC:
2024:KHC:20694 drivers of both vehicles have no valid and effective Driving Licence to drive the lorry and the petition is bad for non- joinder of necessary and proper parties and the claim made by the claimant is excessive.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.

5. Based on the pleadings, the tribunal framed the following issues:
i) Whether the petitioner proves that on 17.05.2018, at about 5.30am., he was proceeding by driving the container lorry bearing Registration No.KA.19.C.9602 from Nanjanagudu to Mangalore via Madierei, and near Boyikeri village at Madikeri, the driver of the lorry bearing Registration No.AP.20.TA.2526, drove the same from opposite side in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the said container lorry and due to the said accident, he has sustained injuries?
ii) Whether the 2nd respondent proves that, the drivers of both vehicles were not having a valid and effective Driving Licence to drive the said vehicles at the time of accident?
NC: 2024:KHC:20694 iii) Whether the petition is bad for non- joinder of necessary parties i.e., the owner and insurer of the container lorry bearing Registration No.KA.19.C.9602 and the driver of the lorry bearing Registration No.AP.20.TA.2526?
iv ) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what amount, from whom?
v) What order or award?
6. In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, claimant got himself examined as PW.1 and also examined a Doctor as PW.2 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P16 and Exs.C1 to C4.

Except filing statement or cross-examining the witness, respondent No.2-Insurance Company has not led any evidence except marking the Insurance Policy as Ex.R1.
7.

On the basis of material evidence, both oral and documentary and on hearing the submissions of learned counsels for both parties, the tribunal answered Issue No.1 in the affirmative, Issue Nos.2 The Manager vs Prasad on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183616186/
3 and 3 in the Negative NC: 2024:KHC:20694 against the respondents and awarded Rs.10,48,800/-
together with interest at the rate of 7% per annum.
8. Being aggrieved by the judgment and award passed by the tribunal, the Insurance Company preferred this appeal.

9. The learned counsel for the appellant-insurer seriously contended that the tribunal committed an error in awarding exorbitant compensation by ignoring the head on collusion and in not apportioning the liability.
There is contributory negligence on the part of the both the drivers of the vehicles.
The income is also taken at Rs.18,000/- per month, which is not correct.

As per the Doctor,
the fractures are united.
Therefore, there is no loss of future income to the claimant due to the disability.
Under other heads also, the tribunal awarded exorbitant compensation.
He further contends that PW.2-Doctor stated the disability at 25%.
However, the tribunal has taken the disability of 25% to the whole body, which is not correct.
Therefore, it would be appropriate to divide the disability by 1/3 rd.
NC: 2024:KHC:20694 Hence, he prays to allow the appeal by reducing the compensation awarded by the tribunal.
10. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent-claimant supports the impugned judgment and award passed by the tribunal and he contended that the claimant was a driver.

Due to the disability suffered, he cannot drive the vehicle and even if he is given any alternative job, his future prospects would be affected and under other heads, the compensation awarded by the tribunal is just and proper.
There is no need to reduce the same.

He further contends that as far as the liability is concerned, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Andhra Pradesh lorry who comes from the opposite direction on the right side of the road.

The charge sheet has also been filed against him and there is no evidence led by respondents to prove their contention by examining the driver of the lorry and no other independent witness are examined.
Therefore, NC: 2024:KHC:20694 there is no question of contributory negligence.

Hence,
he prays for dismissal of the appeal.

11. Having heard the arguments and perused the materials on record, the following points that would arise for consideration are:
i) Whether the appellant proves that there is contributory negligence on the part of the drivers of both lorries?
 ii) Whether the quantum of  compensation awarded by the tribunal is exorbitant and excessive, it needs to reduced?
iii) If so, what order?

4 12.

On perusal of the records, the tribunal framed the issues, especially Issue Nos.2 and 3 cast upon the respondents regarding contention taken by the respondents that there was contributory negligence on the part of the both the drivers and the drivers are not having any valid and effective Driving License.

Except making the contention and marking Ex.R1-Insurance Policy, the NC:
2024:KHC:20694 respondent-Insurance Company has not led any evidence before the tribunal.

13. Though it is contented by the learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurance Company that both lorries were collided with each other, which is head on collision, therefore, the contributory negligence has been fixed on both the vehicles.

In this regard, it is brought to the notice of the Court by learned counsel for claimant that Ex.P4, which is a Police document and the sketch prepared by the Police reveals the accident spot road leading from East to West.
A white line is there in the middle of the road dividing the said road.
Both the vehicles were found standing on the extreme left side of the road.

The container of the claimant was going towards west, which should be on the left side and lorry belongs to Andhra Pradesh required to come by right side i.e., coming from west to east, but the offending vehicle belongs to the Insurance Company is standing just opposite to the road on the extreme right side, which ipso facto reveals this - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:20694 accident was occurred purely due to the rash and negligence driving the lorry by its driver bearing registration No.AP.20.TA.2526.
The Police after investigation filed the charge sheet against Andhra Pradesh vehicle which solely caused the accident occurred on that day.
Therefore, the tribunal has rightly held that the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent of the Andhra Pradesh lorry driver, but not due to the driving of the claimant.
There is no evidence adduced by the lorry driver and any independent witness by the Insurance Company to prove their contention.
14. When such being the case, merely taking contention in the objection statement is not sufficient to prove the case of contributory negligence.
Therefore, I am of the view that appellant-Insurance Company is failed to show that the accident was occurred due to the negligence of both the drivers.
Hence, I answer point No.1 in the negative as against the appellant-Insurance Company.
Now coming to aspect of quantum of compensation, the claimant claims that he is a driver by profession and he is earning more than Rs.21,000/- as per the salary certificate.
Admittedly, the accident was occurred when the claimant was driving the container lorry.

The salary certificate is marked, where there is statutory deduction of Rs.200/- towards Professional Tax and Rs.294/-
towards ESI.
The claimant was working in a registered company namely, Southern Translinks Transport Fleet Owners.
Though the owner was not examined, but the fact remains that the vehicle belongs to the said company.
When the same met with an accident and the claimant was the driver of that Company, disputing the same is not correct.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company has contented that the notional income of Rs.12,500/- has to be considered.
It is not the case for settlement before Lok Adalat to take the notional income as per the chart of the Legal Services Authority.

When the - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:20694 accident was occurred during employment, the vehicle belongs to the employer and the claimant being the driver of the same, the tribunal ought to have taken Rs.21,121/-
as income for per month including the bata as per the salary certificate produced at Ex.P12, but the tribunal considered only Rs.18,000/- per month as income.
17. The tribunal awarded Rs.83,000/- towards pain and suffering.
However, the claimant suffered fracture of both right and left limbs apart from other injuries.
There is multiple fracture injuries and he was admitted in the Hospital totally for 26 days.
Therefore, the compensation awarded under this head does not call for interference.
18. The tribunal awarded Rs.6,773/- towards medical expenses, as claimed and it does not call for interference.

19. The tribunal awarded Rs.72,000/- towards loss of income during laid up period calculating 4 months - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC:20694 income at Rs.18,000/- per month, which does not call for interference.
20.

The tribunal awarded Rs.30,000/- towards special diet, nourishment and attendant charges,
Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses, Rs.7,000/- towards traveling expenses, Rs.20,000/-
towards future unhappiness and loss of amenities, which are just and reasonable and the same do not call for interference.
21.
The tribunal awarded Rs.8,10,000/- towards loss of future income due to disability.
The only important contention is loss of future income due to disability.
PW.2- Doctor has opined the disability of 25% to the limb.
He also stated that there is fracture of right tibia as well as left tibia and they are united.

However, it would be difficult to the claimant to stand for long duration,
climbing steps and there is restriction of left knee and right ankle movements.
In the cross-examination, it was admitted by PW.2-Doctor the unite of the bones were satisfactory and the bones also united as per the X-ray reports.
The - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC:20694 assessment was done by the Doctor as per the guidelines issued by the Central Government.

Except this admission, there is nothing brought on record to show that it would not difficult for the claimant to drive the lorry as he was driving prior to the occurrence of The Manager vs Prasad on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183616186/
6 accident.
22.
Though the learned counsel for the appellant- Insurance Company contends that the claimant has not lost the job and he has been continuing to work in the said Company.
However, he has not produced any document to establish the same.
When the claimant is a permanent employee and he would be entitled to PF, ESI and other benefits, the question of leaving the job by the claimant does not arises.

Due to the occurrence of accident, even the claimant cannot drive the lorry as it is a heavy goods vehicle for long distance, he may be provided an alternate job like cleaner or helper in the Company.
Therefore, there is definitely permanent functional disability to the claimant.

Normally,
the Courts used to consider the disability to the whole body by dividing the disability to the - 15 - NC: 2024:KHC:20694 particular limb by 1/3rd.
However, there are two fractures in both limbs.
When such being the case, the Court cannot take 1/3rd as contended by the learned counsel for appellant-Insurance Company.
If the claimant suffered disability to 25% to the one limb, 50% of disability would come to both limbs.
If disability is assessed at 50% and 1/3rd is divided on the same, it would come to 18%.
However, the tribunal considered 25%, which is just and proper and the same does not call for interference.
23. Accordingly, I pass the following:-
ORDER The appeal filed by the Insurance Company is devoid of merits.

Accordingly,
the same is dismissed.
The amount in deposit is ordered to be transferred to the tribunal.
